evidence.snippet:
Amends: [2026-11-13-shared-record-behind-a-store-port.md](2026-11-13-shared-record-behind-a-store-port.md), the record-size limit. Every store refuses a record past `recordLimit`, and a refused record never lists; a batch may still land in part, as the port allows.

## Problem

Every record store refuses a record past core's `recordLimit`, 4 MiB. A head that changes many workspace manifests makes one guardrails finding per manifest, each naming the scripts it changes, and their record can pass the limit. The store then refused the round's records after the harness had stored a verdict of findings, so the review threw a store error with that verdict standing.

Example: 1,500 changed manifests, each naming twenty long scripts, wrote a guardrails record of about 5 MB.

## Choice

- Past the limit, the guardrails check leaves out the detail of its last findings in ID order, as `SightingBudget.checkRecord.fit` does. A trimmed finding keeps its ID, rule, severity, resolution, place and What to do, so what blocks is unchanged. Its Why here names how many files lost their detail and says that `git diff` shows them. A finding that trimming would not make smaller keeps its detail.

CI runs `npm run check` from the head's own `package.json`. So a head that rewrites that script makes the gate do less, or nothing, and CI still reads green. Melian's notice on a changed `package.json` said only which analyser the file configures. It named a switch-off only when the head deleted the file.

Example: a head changes `"check": "biome check … && vitest --run"` to `"check": "true"`. Every CI job passes, and the notice gave no sign that the gate's own command changed.

## Rule

`switchOffs` in `packages/core/src/analyser.ts` names each script the base's `package.json` had that the head changes or removes. It reads any `package.json` in any letter case of the name, but guardrails passes it only the manifests its notice already covers: the root's and each workspace package's. A script whose value differs as JSON is changed. A script missing from the head's `scripts`, or every script when the head's `scripts` is absent or not an object, is removed. A script the head only adds, and a change to any other field, add nothing. It reads both revisions as npm's `json-parse-even-better-errors` does: it strips one leading byte order mark, then calls `JSON.parse`. It does not use the JSON-with-comments reader of the tsconfig and Biome checks. That reader drops a comma before `}` or `]` even inside a string, so `"echo ,}"` and `"echo }"` read as the same script. When the base had scripts and the head's file does not read as a JSON object, the notice says Melian cannot read the head's scripts. That covers a malformed file, a file too large to read, and a symbolic link, whose blob is its target's path though npm follows it to a file whose scripts run.

Every script counts, not only those a workflow or another script runs. The issue asked that this be read from the authority, the workflows and the scripts, rather than a hand-kept list of names. No such reading is complete:
- `npm run check` also runs `precheck` and `postcheck`;
- npm runs lifecycle scripts such as `prepare` and `postinstall` that no cal [cut at 2 KiB]

verification.reason: Traced in code. runCheck passes every check's findings through SightingBudget.checkRecord.fit (checks.ts:327). Past the limit, fit sorts by ID and abridges every finding after the latest cut that fits (sighting-budget.ts:46-107). The root package.json notice has no priority or exemption. Finding.abridged (findings.ts:1947-1957) replaces `what` with the shorter plain message ("Review the change to package.json, which configures …") and `whyHere` with the note. That drops the switch-off sentence ("It changes the npm script \"check\"") that the base decision 2026-11-20-every-npm-script-is-a-switch-off requires the notice to name. That base decision also dealt with the 4 MiB limit already, by quoting at most ten names per sentence. The head decision guardrails-record-fits-the-store amends only the shared-record decision and gives no Amends or Supersedes link to the switch-off decision. Its trimming therefore departs from a base decision whose reason still holds: the maintainer should see that CI's gate command changed. Blocking stays unchanged, as both decisions say, so the loss is information, not the verdict. It needs a record over 4 MiB, and the head author controls how many manifests it changes.

evidence.snippet: - **A projection larger than the local findings.** For Biome and tsc, the projected fixed sentences are longer than the local text: 518 bytes against 487 for one finding's message and explanation. A static check whose local findings come within about 6% of the limit can pass the budget while its exported record is past it. The store then refuses the record after the verdict is stored. The reader sees a store error with exit code 2, and no verdict in CI.

verification.reason: The bound is measured on the wrong thing. `fit` (sighting-budget.ts:51-60) sums the canonical JSON of the local findings and returns them unchanged when that fits. `runCheck` (checks.ts:322-328) applies it to every check. At export, `sighting()` in review-records.ts:431-440 rewrites each static finding's message and explanation to the fixed `withheld` sentences. Those are longer than the local Biome/tsc text; the head's own decision doc puts one finding at 518 bytes against 487. `storable()` (record.ts:327-329), called from every store's `add`, then throws once the projected record passes `recordLimit`. That happens after adjudication has stored the verdict, so the review fails with a store error. Nothing in the code remeasures the projected record. The head's decision doc lists this under "Known limits" (lines 32-33), which states the failure; it does not prevent it. The doc names issue #626 as the future fix. The scenario's wording is slightly off: the maintainer's ruling covers the guardrails record, and extending the budget to other checks is the builder's choice (doc line 17). The defect is still real in the head's added bound.
